chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Chick's library and Sampson's tunes in the book
summary: On joining the band McRae found enough music for two books, with Henderson charts and Sampson arrangements.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Now when I came back from off the road with Lil Armstrong in '36, I joined Chick that spring of '36.

That's when I joined Chick at the Savoy. We was getting ready to go on that -- one nighters. String of Singing one nighters all out down South and through the West for a few months -- and things like that.
And that's when I found out that he had all this music. He had enough music for two books, because he had a lot of Fletcher Henderson things.
And Charlie Dixon had made a lot of things. He had bought arrangements from other people. Like Jimmy Mundy had made some things for him.

And he was like -- Anybody came along with a good arrangement, if he liked it he would buy it, you know.
And he had a lot of music in his book. But he also had Sampson in there who was writing a lot of arrangements for him.
When I first joined the band, they wasn't playing "Stompin At The Savoy." Just was another arrangement in the book.
